arxiv-1606-02096.title: Towards Playlist Generation Algorithms Using RNNs Trained on Within-Track Transitions Conference: Workshop on Surprise, Opposition, and Obstruction in Adaptive and Personalized Systems (SOAP) June 13–17, 2016, Halifax, NS, Canada Note: This work was part funded by the “Fusing Audio and Semantic Tech
arxiv-1606-02096.creator: Keunwoo Choi György Fazekas Mark Sandler
arxiv-1606-02096.description: Abstract We introduce a novel playlist generation algorithm that focuses on the quality of transitions using a recurrent neural network (RNN). The proposed model assumes that optimal transitions between tracks can be modelled and predicted by internal transitions within music tracks.

arxiv-1712-06447.title: The one-dimensional asymmetric persistent random walk
arxiv-1712-06447.creator: Vincent Rossetto
arxiv-1712-06447.description: Abstract Persistent random walks are intermediate transport processes between a uniform rectilinear motion and a Brownian motion. They are formed by successive steps of random finite lengths and directions travelled at a fixed speed. The isotropic and symmetric one-dimensional persistent random walk is governed by the telegrapher’s equation, also called hyperbolic heat conduction equation.

arxiv-1808-09839.title: Botnet Campaign Detection on Twitter
arxiv-1808-09839.creator: Jeremy D. Fields a,b a Department of Computer Science, SUNY Polytechnic, Marcy, NY b Critical Technologies Inc, 1001 Broad St, Utica, NY
arxiv-1808-09839.description: Abstract This is an approach to detecting a subset of bots on Twitter, that at best is under-researched. This approach will be generic enough to be adaptable to most, if not all social networks. The subset of bots this focuses on are those that can evade most, if not all current detection methods.

arxiv-2102-12842.title: Coalgebra Encoding for Efficient Minimization
arxiv-2102-12842.creator: Hans-Peter Deifel, Stefan Milius, Thorsten Wißmann
arxiv-2102-12842.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hans-Peter Deifel, Stefan Milius, Thorsten Wißmann. Recently, we have developed an efficient generic partition refinement algorithm, which computes behavioural equivalence on a state-based system given as an encoded coalgebra, and implemented it in the tool CoPaR. Here we extend this to a fully fledged minimization algorithm and tool by integrating two new aspects: (1) the computation of the transition structure on the minimized state set, and (2) the computation of the reachable part of the given system.

arxiv-2107-09829.title: Gamma mixed fractional Lévy Ornstein - Uhlenbeck process
arxiv-2107-09829.creator: Héctor Araya Johanna Garzón Rolando Rubilar
arxiv-2107-09829.description: Abstract In this article, we introduce a non Gaussian long memory process constructed by the aggregation of independent copies of a fractional Lévy Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with random coefficients. Several properties and a limit theorem are studied for this new process. Finally, some simulations of the limit process are shown. 2010 AMS Classification Numbers: 60G10, 60G17, 60H05, 60H30.

arxiv-2110-04471.title: Provably Efficient Black-Box Action Poisoning Attacks Against Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2110-04471.creator: Guanlin Liu, Lifeng Lai
arxiv-2110-04471.description: Abstract Due to the broad range of applications of reinforcement learning (RL), understanding the effects of adversarial attacks against RL model is essential for the safe applications of this model. Prior theoretical works on adversarial attacks against RL mainly focus on either observation poisoning attacks or environment poisoning attacks.

arxiv-2210-15531.title: Anisotropic Proximal Gradient
arxiv-2210-15531.creator: Emanuel Laude, Panagiotis Patrinos
arxiv-2210-15531.description: Abstract This paper studies a novel algorithm for nonconvex composite minimization which can be interpreted in terms of dual space nonlinear preconditioning for the classical proximal gradient method. The proposed scheme can be applied to additive composite minimization problems whose smooth part exhibits an anisotropic descent inequality relative to a reference function.

arxiv-2302-09574.title: Guided Deep Kernel Learning
arxiv-2302-09574.creator: Idan Achituve, Gal Chechik, Ethan Fetaya
arxiv-2302-09574.description: Abstract Combining Gaussian processes with the expressive power of deep neural networks is commonly done nowadays through deep kernel learning (DKL). Unfortunately, due to the kernel optimization process, this often results in losing their Bayesian benefits. In this study, we present a novel approach for learning deep kernels by utilizing infinite-width neural networks.

arxiv-2311-15184.title: Factorial moments of the Poisson distribution of order k k Journal: (internal report CC23-11)
arxiv-2311-15184.creator: S. R. Mane
arxiv-2311-15184.description: Abstract The factorial moments of the standard Poisson distribution are well known. The present note presents an explicit combinatorial sum for the factorial moments of the Poisson distribution of order k k . Unlike the standard Poisson distribution (the case k = 1 k=1 ), for k > 1 k>1 the structure of the factorial moments is much more complicated.

arxiv-2312-10728.title: Benchmarks for Physical Reasoning AI
arxiv-2312-10728.creator: Andrew Melnik andrew.melnik.papers@gmail.com, Robin Schiewer robin.schiewer@ini.rub.de, Moritz Lange moritz.lange@ini.rub.de, Andrei Muresanu andrei.muresanu@uwaterloo.ca, Mozhgan Saeidi mozhgans@stanford.edu, Animesh Garg animesh.garg@gatech.edu, Helge Ritter helge@techfak.uni-bielefeld.de
arxiv-2312-10728.description: Abstract Physical reasoning is a crucial aspect in the development of general AI systems, given that human learning starts with interacting with the physical world before progressing to more complex concepts. Although researchers have studied and assessed the physical reasoning of AI approaches through various specific benchmarks, there is no comprehensive approach to evaluating and measuring progress.

arxiv-2503-02121.title: On the model theory of the Farey graph Thanks: This research was partially funded through the Cluster of Excellence by the German Research Foundation (DFG) under Germany’s Excellence Strategy EXC 2044–390685587, Mathematics Münster: Dynamics–Geometry–Structure and by CRC 1442 Geometry: Deformations
arxiv-2503-02121.creator: Zahra Mohammadi Khangheshlaghi & Katrin Tent
arxiv-2503-02121.description: Abstract . We axiomatize the theory of the Farey graph and prove that it is ω \omega -stable of Morley rank ω \omega . 1. Introduction Our purpose in this article is to investigate the model-theoretic properties of the Farey graph, a combinatorial and geometric structure that arises in a number of mathematical fields.

arxiv-2503-07470.title: Advancing Vietnamese Information Retrieval with Learning Objective and Benchmark
arxiv-2503-07470.creator: Phu-Vinh Nguyen, Minh-Nam Tran, Long Nguyen, Dien Dinh
arxiv-2503-07470.description: Abstract With the rapid development of natural language processing, many language models have been invented for multiple tasks. One important task is information retrieval (IR), which requires models to retrieve relevant documents. Despite its importance in many real-life applications, especially in retrieval augmented generation (RAG) systems, this task lacks Vietnamese benchmarks.

arxiv-2507-00743.title: TUNABLE WAVELET UNIT BASED CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK IN OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY ANALYSIS ENHANCEMENT FOR CLASSIFYING TYPE OF EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE SURGERY Thanks: This article has been supported in part by UCSD Vision Research Center Core Grant P30EY022589, NIH grant R01EY016323, NIH Grant R01
arxiv-2507-00743.creator: An Le 1 , Nehal Mehta 2 , William Freeman 2 , Ines Nagel 2 , Melanie Tran 2 , Anna Heinke 2 , Akshay Agnihotri 2 , Lingyun Cheng 2 , Dirk-Uwe Bartsch 2 , Hung Nguyen 1 , Truong Nguyen 1 , Cheolhong An 1
arxiv-2507-00743.description: Abstract In this study, we developed deep learning-based method to classify the type of surgery performed for epiretinal membrane (ERM) removal—either internal limiting membrane (ILM) removal or ERM-alone removal. Our model, based on the ResNet18 convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, utilizes postoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT) center scans as inputs.

arxiv-2507-08440.title: Finding Common Ground: Using Large Language Models to Detect Agreement in Multi-Agent Decision Conferences
arxiv-2507-08440.creator: Selina Heller, Mohamed Ibrahim, David Antony Selby, Sebastian Vollmer
arxiv-2507-08440.description: Abstract Decision conferences are structured, collaborative meetings that bring together experts from various fields to address complex issues and reach a consensus on recommendations for future actions or policies. These conferences often rely on facilitated discussions to ensure productive dialogue and collective agreement.

pmc-10703914.title: First isolation of Mycobacterium saskatchewanense from medical devices
pmc-10703914.creator: Francesco Bisognin, Vincenzo Ferraro, Federica Sorella, Giulia Lombardi, Tiziana Lazzarotto, Paola Dal Monte
pmc-10703914.description: Mycobacterium saskatchewanense is a species of pigmented slow-growing Non-Tuberculous Mycobacteria (NTM), positive for Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) by AccuProbe system. MAC organisms have frequently been isolated from different medical devices. This is the first study reporting isolation of M. saskatchewanense from medical devices and highlights the importance of correctly identifying the NTMs that often colonize sanitary water.

pmc-10742049.title: Evaluation of Potential Predictive Biomarkers for Defining Brain Radiotherapy Efficacy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients with Brain Metastases: A Case Report and a Narrative Review
pmc-10742049.creator: Angelo Luciano, Luigi Liguori, Giovanna Polcaro, Francesco Sabbatino, Stefano Pepe, Dirk Rades
pmc-10742049.description: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the second most common cancer worldwide, resulting in 1.8 million deaths per year. Most patients are diagnosed with a metastatic disease. Brain metastases are one of the most common metastatic sites and are associated with severe neurological symptoms, shorter survival, and the worst clinical outcomes.

pmc-10861241.title: Coupled catalytic states and the role of metal coordination in Cas9
pmc-10861241.creator: Anuska Das, Jay Rai, Mitchell O. Roth, Yuerong Shu, Megan L. Medina, Mackenzie R. Barakat, Hong Li
pmc-10861241.description: Controlling the activity of the CRISPR–Cas9 system is essential to its safe adoption for clinical and research applications. Although the conformational dynamics of Cas9 are known to control its enzymatic activity, details of how Cas9 influences the catalytic processes at both nuclease domains remain elusive.

pmc-11325708.title: Guide to extraluminal fish bone retrieval with serial computed tomography scans: a case series
pmc-11325708.creator: Ting Ting Yew, Ing Ping Tang, Li Yun Lim, Yuanzhi Cheah, Shiong Leong Yew
pmc-11325708.description: BackgroundFish bone ingestion is commonly encountered in emergency department. It poses a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge particularly when it migrates extraluminally, necessitating a comprehensive and multidisciplinary approach for successful management.Case presentationHere we reported four cases of extraluminal fish bone. The first patient was a 68-year-old Chinese man who had odynophagia shortly after a meal involving fish.

pmc-11541216.title: Efficient conversion of syngas to linear α-olefins by phase-pure χ-Fe5C2
pmc-11541216.creator: Peng Wang, Fu-Kuo Chiang, Jiachun Chai, A Iulian Dugulan, Juan Dong, Wei Chen, Robin J P Broos, Bo Feng, Yuanjun Song, Yijun Lv, Quan Lin, Rongming Wang, Ivo A W Filot, Zhuowu Men, Emiel J M Hensen
pmc-11541216.description: Oil has long been the dominant feedstock for producing fuels and chemicals, but coal, natural gas and biomass are increasingly explored alternatives1–3. Their conversion first generates syngas, a mixture of CO and H2, which is then processed further using Fischer–Tropsch (FT) chemistry. However, although commercial FT technology for fuel production is established, using it to access valuable chemicals remains challenging.

pmc-11593057.title: An Animal Ex Vivo Model Comparing Two Different Methods of Sinus Floor Elevation with Great Elevation Heights: Macroscopic, Microscopic and Radiological Analysis
pmc-11593057.creator: Erick Rafael Fernández Castellano, Lorena Benito Garzón, Magaly Teresa Márquez Sánchez, Javier Flores-Fraile
pmc-11593057.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Maxillary sinus pneumatization increases with age and tooth loss, leading to a reduction in the maxillary alveolar ridge, which often results in insufficient bone height for the proper placement of dental implants. This study focused on performing maxillary sinus elevations in ex vivo bisected pig heads using novel access and elevation devices, comparing these with the osteotome sinus floor elevation (OSFE) technique. Materials and Methods:An experimental study was conducted using 20 ex vivo adult pig heads.

pmc-11603923.title: Evaluation of high school-based dengue solution model in Southern Thailand: a community participatory action research
pmc-11603923.creator: Charuai Suwanbamrung, Sandeep Kumar Mehraj, Melkamu Worku Kercho, Muhammad Haroon Stanikzai, Temesgen Anjulo Ageru, Jiraporn Jaroenpool, Panatda Pibul, Shamarina Shohaimi, Eskinder Israel
pmc-11603923.description: IntroductionBy the time the globe started to tackle the COVID-19 pandemic, Southeast Asian countries had faced an increased dengue incidence, which has eventually become an important public health problem. However, effective and sustainable disease control measures in the area are still lacking.

pmc-11691182.title: ADAPTING TO HEALTH CHANGE: STUDENT RESPONSES TO DIFFERENT DELIVERY MODALITIES
pmc-11691182.creator: Keith Kleszynski, Lee Jennings, Shirley James
pmc-11691182.description: BackgroundAdapting to Health Change (AHC) is a two-hour aging sensitivity simulation training designed to improve student empathy and understanding of common age- and chronic illness-related functional changes. AHC includes role-play with props and 4 activity stations: hearing loss, neuropathy and dexterity, vision loss and medication management, and mobility and transfer. Training is facilitated by interdisciplinary faculty and staff.

pmc-12467771.title: An Assessment of the Effective Pollination Period and Its Main Limiting Factor in Wurfbainia villosa var. villosa (Lour.) Škorničk. & A. D. Poulsen (Zingiberaceae)
pmc-12467771.creator: Qianxia Li, Yanqian Wang, Ge Li, Shuang Li, Hongyou Zhao, Chunyong Yang, Zhibing Guan, Yating Zhu, Lin Xiao, Yanfang Wang, Lixia Zhang
pmc-12467771.description: Simple SummaryWurfbainia villosa var. villosa is cultivated for its fruits, which are mainly used as a traditional Chinese medicine and a cardamom-like spice. However, low fruit set is a problem, with the effective pollination period (EPP, defined as the window during which flowers can be fertilized) being a key factor.

pmc-12759454.title: Development and Validation of a Fall Detection System for Older Adults Who Use Wheelchairs
pmc-12759454.creator: Laura Rice, David Peeler, Peter Presti, Andrea Tangonan
pmc-12759454.description: Falls are a concern for the 1 million older adults who use a wheelchairs or scooters (WC/S) in the US. ∼60% of the population are affected by falls. After a fall, people who use WC/S spend an average of 9 minutes (range: 1-45 min) on the floor and 80% require assistance to recover.

pmc-13193338.title: Medication error reporting in Ghana: A multicenter assessment of healthcare professionals’ knowledge, attitudes and practices
pmc-13193338.creator: Stephen Mensah Arhin, Isaac Tabiri Henneh, Kwasi Sobre Nkrumah, Ewura Seidu Yahaya, Phyllis Elsie Owusu Agyei, Meshack Antwi-Adjei, Martins Ekor, Douglas Aninng Opoku, Douglas Aninng Opoku, Douglas Aninng Opoku, Douglas Aninng Opoku, Douglas Aninng Opoku, Douglas Aninng Opoku, Douglas Aninng Opoku,
pmc-13193338.description: BackgroundMedication errors (MEs) remain a leading cause of preventable patient harm globally, with significant implications in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where reporting systems are not standardized. Understanding healthcare professionals’ knowledge, attitudes and practices is critical to designing interventions that strengthen patient safety.MethodsA cross-sectional, multicenter study was conducted among healthcare professionals, including nurses, doctors, and pharmacists.

pmc-13530575.title: Poster 98. HTO Provides Lower Two-Year TKA Conversion Risk Than UKA in All Ages
pmc-13530575.creator: Reza Katanbaf, Monica Misch, Oliver Sax, Drew Saltzman, Anthony Velott, Craig Bennett

pmc-13536847.creator: Christina N Bobrek, Claudia R Silver, Zade Moureiden, Cynthia Samra, Anastasia Peele
